result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A is cleaner to glance at: every block is in call order with minute marks, the cost questions are tight, and the close books a named decision-maker on a date. But apart from job cost, draws and bonding, its content could fit any service. B is longer and puts its minute marks in a separate clock rather than on each section, but it is clearly written for subcontractors (WIP, over/under billings, retainage, lien waivers, certified payroll), has a strong cost-of-the-problem section, and closes with a decision-maker blank and a dated next step. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B fits the main need better: each section has its own minute mark and a few short prompts, so a nervous caller can quickly find their place, and its close names the decision-maker and pins a date. A is far more specific to subcontractors (WIP, over/under billings, retainage, lien waivers, certified payroll), but its timing only appears in a separate clock block, and its long question bank, separate objection list and signals list make it harder to scan mid-call. B is weak on construction detail, never mentioning retainage or progress billing, and neither answer brings up the owner doing the books at night.
